question: A beam of light falls on a metal surface such that photo-electrons are generated. If power of the light source starts to decrease linearly with time $t$, then variation of the photocurrent $I$ and magnitude of the stopping potential $|V|$ with time is best represented by :
solution:
The frequency of the light does not change, only its power (intensity).

Photocurrent is proportional to the number of photons arriving per second, which is proportional to the power. So $I$ decreases linearly with time.

The stopping potential depends only on the frequency: $e|V| = h\nu - \phi$. So $|V|$ stays constant.

The graph with $I$ decreasing linearly and $|V|$ constant is option (1).
